#!/bin/bash
# namd examples: https://stfc.service-now.com/hartreecentre?id=kb_article&sys_id=1c8b4bfcdb440c5034836c16ca961930
# https://www.ibm.com/support/knowledgecenter/en/SSETD4_9.1.3/lsf_command_ref/bsub.heading_options.1.html

#FLUX --job-name=respties
#FLUX -o std.{id}.o
#FLUX -e std.{id}.e

# LSF '-R "span[ptile=64]"' and '-n 128' requests 128 tasks distributed
# across nodes such that each node gets 64 tasks. This is equivalent
# to 2 nodes, each with 64 tasks.
#FLUX --nodes=2
#FLUX --ntasks-per-node=64

#FLUX --queue=compbiomed
#FLUX -t 1:00
#FLUX --exclusive

# go to the right directionary
cd $HCBASE/resp/tyk2_l5_l16

source /etc/profile.d/modules.sh
module load namd-gcc/2.12
#module load namd/2.13

# The LSF environment variables and manual task counting are replaced by
# Flux's own environment variables and automatic resource management.

echo "lsb hosts:"
# The LSF variable $LSB_HOSTS is replaced with the Flux equivalent.
echo $FLUX_JOB_NODELIST

NP=64
BASE_DIR=`pwd`

function schedule_system() {
    local lambda=$1
	local replica=$2

	echo "Scheduling ligand and complex for lambda $lambda replica $replica"
	LIG_PATH="lig/lambda_$lambda/rep$replica"
	COMPLEX_PATH="complex/lambda_$lambda/rep$replica"
	# We use timeout to ensure that each NAMD ligand process is terminated in case it gets stuck
    # 60 seconds * 60 minutes * 4 hours = 4 hours timeout for the ligand
    local LIG_TIMEOUT=$(( 60 * 60 * 4 ))

    # move to the correct ligand directory
    cd $BASE_DIR
    cd $LIG_PATH
	(

	    # first is the ligand part with the timeout
#	    ( timeout $LIG_TIMEOUT flux run -n $NP namd2    min.namd > min.log &&
#        flux run -n $NP namd2    eq_step1.namd > eq_step1.log &&
#        flux run -n $NP namd2    eq_step2.namd > eq_step2.log &&
#        flux run -n $NP namd2    eq_step3.namd > eq_step3.log &&
#        flux run -n $NP namd2    eq_step4.namd > eq_step4.log &&
#        flux run -n $NP namd2    prod.namd > prod.log &&
#        echo "Finished ligand: lambda $lambda replica $replica"
#        ) ;
        (
        # then the complex part, no timeout
        cd $BASE_DIR && cd $COMPLEX_PATH &&
        # 'mpiexec' is replaced by 'flux run'
        flux run -n $NP namd2    min.namd > min.log &&
        flux run -n $NP namd2    eq_step1.namd > eq_step1.log &&
        flux run -n $NP namd2    eq_step2.namd > eq_step2.log &&
        flux run -n $NP namd2    eq_step3.namd > eq_step3.log &&
        flux run -n $NP namd2    eq_step4.namd > eq_step4.log &&
        flux run -n $NP namd2    prod.namd > prod.log &&
        echo "Finished complex: lambda $lambda replica $replica"
        )
    ) & 
}

#declare -a lambdas=(0.00 0.05 0.10 0.20 0.30 0.40 0.50 0.60 0.70 0.80 0.90 0.95 1.00)
#declare -a replicas=(1 2 3 4 5)

declare -a lambdas=(0.60)
declare -a replicas=(1 2)

for lambda in "${lambdas[@]}"; do
    for replica in "${replicas[@]}"; do
       schedule_system $lambda $replica
    done
done

wait

issues: The script's first action is `cd $HCBASE/resp/tyk2_l5_l16`. This relies on the environment variable `$HCBASE` being correctly set in the job's execution environment. If `$HCBASE` is not set or is incorrect, the script will fail to change to the intended directory, which will likely cause all subsequent file-based operations and simulation runs to fail with 'file not found' errors.
